Subject: Dedicated capacity questions + migration economics

Hi Marissa,

We're evaluating moving a portion of our traffic from Redwood's hosted API to Dedicated capacity (mainly for predictable latency and data isolation). Before we schedule a deep-dive, could you help clarify a few items so we can scope internally?

- GPU pool sizing: How do you recommend sizing N GPUs for our peak load — we see 600 RPS of short-chat generation with 1.2k token/session average.
- Throughput guarantees: What SLAs do you offer for sustained throughput? Any hard throttling thresholds we should plan for?
- Reserved commits: If we do a 12-month commit vs 24-month, what typical discounts apply and how flexible are start dates?
- Migration credits: We have $120k of remaining hosted credits. Do you offer conversion credits or bridge months during migration?

Our procurement timeline is April/May, so an early sense of numbers would be ideal. Happy to loop in engineering after you share the baseline.

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and then propose a short call (30 mins) to align on traffic shape.

1) GPU pool sizing: Ballpark we typically map 1 A100-80GB-equivalent GPU to ~250–400 peak token/sec for chat-style workloads with KV-cache enabled. For your 600 RPS of short-chat, my rough calc suggests starting with a 2-GPU pool (capacity headroom for bursts) and an autoscaling buffer to 3 GPUs for sustained spikes. We'll validate with your sequence-length distribution.

2) Throughput guarantees: Our Dedicated offering includes a throughput monitoring SLA; we guarantee provisioned throughput within ±10% and provide automatic burst handling up to 1.5x for short intervals. We include throttling thresholds in the config; we can set a hard cap per-customer if you need strict limits.

3) Reserved commits: Typical pricing tiers are 12-month (baseline), 24-month (additional discount). Discounts vary by commit level — I'll share a sample pricing spreadsheet. Start dates are flexible within a 90-day window from contract signature.

4) Migration credits & bridge months: We do offer conversion credits for remaining hosted balances on a case-by-case basis and sometimes provide 1–2 bridge months at no charge for larger deals. I'll have Aditya draft concrete proposals.

Can you confirm timezone availability for a 30-min call next week (PST preferred)?

Best,
Marissa Cole

Hi Olivia — looping in some preliminary numbers so you have concrete items to discuss internally. Attached: redwood_dedicated_pricing_v1.xlsx and migration_credits_summary.pdf.

Summary highlights:
- Recommended baseline: 2 x A100-80GB equiv GPUs; expected sustained throughput ~500–700 RPS depending on batching and prompt length.
- Throughput SLA options:
  • Bronze: best-effort with alerting (no SLA)
  • Silver: 99.5% provisioning availability for configured throughput (recommended)
  • Gold: 99.9% with priority routing and guaranteed burst credit (enterprise)
- Pricing/commits (examples):
  • 12-month commit: list price less 18% standard commit discount
  • 24-month commit: list price less 26%
  • Add-on: burst pool capacity (billed on usage)
- Migration economics:
  • Conversion credit: We can convert up to 50% of remaining hosted credits to Dedicated committed dollars (applied pro-rata across the first N months).
  • Bridge months: For deals > $200k ARR, we typically offer 1 month free as a bridge; exceptions possible with commercial approval.

Open questions we need from your side:
- Typical token distribution (input/output tokens per request) and percent of peak traffic in 95th percents.
- Desired commit term (12 vs 24) and target monthly spend for budgeting.

If these look reasonable I can turn this into a formal quote and proposed contract language.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao

Thanks Aditya — this is helpful. A few follow-ups after reviewing the sheet:

- We'd like to avoid a large upfront commit. Would Redwood consider applying conversion credits to allow a lower initial committed spend (effectively offsetting month 1–3)?
- Can the bridge month be extended to 2 months if we commit to 24 months? That would make our procurement ask much easier to justify.
- For throughput SLA: the 99.5% Silver tier is likely sufficient, but would you include hard throttling thresholds in the contract language? We're especially concerned about peak bursts during market-open (short 10–15 minute surges).

Also, two procurement items: an initial PO value and an internal legal redline window (we need the contract for review by 10 Apr). Looking forward to the formal quote.

Best,
Olivia
